about: The review of each map's exact bytes (docs/decisions/0017-a-map-change-carries-a-review-of-its-bytes.md). tools/check-map-review.py fails any map whose sha256 is not the one recorded here.

exemption.reason: Grandfathered, not reviewed: this map predates the review gate and has never been blind-mapped. examples/faa-part-107/blind-mapping/ reviewed the 2026-01-01 map against the 2026 text; this map was last changed in substance in 5d09898, before those corrections, and nothing compared it with a second reading of the 2020-01-01 text. A blind second mapping is still owed before it is used for the regulation target under #3. Since then one structural change, alongside the 2026 map's (#58, docs/decisions/0020): a top-level `extent` naming the same twelve subpart B sections (§ 107.25, .29, .31, .33, .35, .36, .37, .39, .41, .45, .49, .51), which check-locators-section.py's coverage now requires. No entry changed; the bytes it departs from are sha256 6ceb108a5e2bfe76f275a79cefc4e04b46bb0f173650b17d5f37d776f3ec4edf. It stays `legacy` rather than `non-semantic` because non-semantic names a reviewed map it departs from, and there is none. Since then #117 (docs/decisions/0025): assertedBy on all nine assertion entries, with a sentence in four notes quoting § 107.49's lead-in and in two giving the reason for `caller`. The bytes it departs from are sha256 9cc8577cd14030c61f7027fe813bcc7c6a7697783bbcb823291de9354a8e3afe. That change was read, together with the 2026 map's, by the independent reviewer whose verdict is examples/faa-part-107/independent-verdict-117.json (it names these bytes under `maps`); the map as a whole is still unreviewed, so the exemption stays `legacy`. A third change, for #116 (docs/decisions/0026), adds crossReferences and changes nothing else, departing from 032d4c3adc1c8eb0fa3e5b5c6d35c36a873b5f7b0158da2af9e94c110daf435c. The manifest now declares the CFR's pointerPhrases. Without them the built-in list detected no pointer in this map, and the check now fails that. With them it detected four pointers nobody had declared, and they are answered as the reviewed 2026 map answers the same words: civil-twilight-operation's "paragraph (b) of this section" (unmapped: its own evidence) and "as defined in the Air Almanac" (civil-twilight-alaska), visual-line-of-sight's "the ability described in paragraph (a) of this section" (unaided-visual-contact), and visual-observer-conditions' "in the manner specified in § 107.31" (visual-line-of-sight). This change was not reviewed against the 2020 text; the blind second mapping this exemption owes should cover it. A fourth change applies docs/decisions/0021 to this map from the 2020-01-01 text, departing from bb89e946f4b72f1928a835444b0a99b2f49a1c47e17a53ba15771496df3f8fc7: two scope: out entries, waiver-policy (§ 107.200) and waivable-regulations (§ 107.205, which at this date lists § 107.29 whole and has no (j)), and suspendedBy: [waivable-regulations] on 27 entries; and it reviews the four crossReferences above against the 2020 text, changing civil-twilight-operation's "paragraph (b) of this section" from unmapped to resolvedBy anti-collision-lighting (that entry cites § 107.29(b) and quotes it whole, so the reason was false) and removing a stale sentence from visual-observer-conditions' note. That change was read against the 2020 text by an independent reviewer in a separate context, whose verdict is independent-verdict-2020-waivers.json: 29 of 29 changed or added entries agree, 4 of 4 crossReferences agree, completeness agrees, at these bytes, sha256 ab6e909fa6b538e8d85a1652657e557b4f864ecabc4a4e4f4cdd2591c5b48629. The map as a whole is still not blind-mapped, so the exemption stays legacy; the blind second mapping it owes should also cover the missing entry for § 107.51's introductory text, recorded as unmapped on waivable-regulations.
